We have $n \geq 3$, and $\mathcal{A} = \{\{z_1, \ldots, z_n\} \mid z_i \in \mathbb{C}, |z_i| = 1\}$. We want to find the minimum over all $A \in \mathcal{A}$ of $\max_{|u|=1} \prod_{z \in A} |u - z|$.

So we have $n$ points on the unit circle, and for each such configuration, we look at the maximum over $u$ on the unit circle of the product of distances from $u$ to all the $z_i$. We want to minimize this maximum.

Let me think about this. The product $\prod_{z \in A} |u - z|$ is the absolute value of the polynomial $p(u) = \prod_{z \in A} (u - z)$ evaluated at $u$ on the unit circle.

So we want to minimize $\max_{|u|=1} |p(u)|$ over all monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose roots are all on the unit circle.

By the mean value property or by integration: $\frac{1}{2\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} |p(e^{i\theta})|^2 d\theta = \sum_{k=0}^n |a_k|^2$ where $p(z) = \sum a_k z^k$. For a monic polynomial with roots on the unit circle, $a_n = 1$.
